summary: SL-046 added a breakdown of the scan by kind of file: a fixed extension table (FileKinds), a single-pass KindBreakdown.Compute over the finished store, a ten-row kinds panel, and an additive per-kind-totals `kinds` array in the schema-1 report. It needed two builds. Code review 1 found that Compute threw on compatibility-letter extensions such as the Kelvin sign, which the design's OrdinalIgnoreCase-plus-ToLowerInvariant pairing allowed. Validate reconciled the kinds to the core totals exactly on real C: and D:, and ran a 199,663-check fuzz with 0 failures. No person looked at the panel on screen, and every finding and design question was disposed of by a model.

payload.reason: Nothing blocks the reflection. The on-screen check of the kinds panel and the product choices on Installers, Kelvin-sign extensions, ts and no-extension have no answer from a person, and they are listed as unknowns and candidates rather than treated as settled.
payload.summary: SL-046 added a breakdown of the scan by kind of file: a fixed extension table (FileKinds), a single-pass KindBreakdown.Compute over the finished store, a ten-row kinds panel, and an additive per-kind-totals `kinds` array in the schema-1 report. It needed two builds. Code review 1 found that Compute threw on compatibility-letter extensions such as the Kelvin sign, which the design's OrdinalIgnoreCase-plus-ToLowerInvariant pairing allowed. Validate reconciled the kinds to the core totals exactly on real C: and D:, and ran a 199,663-check fuzz with 0 failures. No person looked at the panel on screen, and every finding and design question was disposed of by a model.
payload.estimate_error: The medium size held: one aggregate, one panel, one report section and 20 tests, and the second build was a three-item fix. The risk was aimed at the wrong precondition. The design imported two must-verify preconditions, totality (O-001) and no writer during the pass (O-002). The critique filed two majors (M1, M2) on O-002, and the code already excludes it: the store is private to Scanner.Run and Cancel waits for Scan to return. Totality is the one that broke, and it was found by code review after build 1 was already green. Medium was enough for tier. A slice that classifies real file names on a real drive should have had a totality or fuzz case in its design cases list. The 14 example-based shapes did not include a name whose case-insensitive miss lowers onto an existing key.

learned.lesson: In this slice the must-verify precondition that failed was totality over real file names. The one the critique attacked, no writer during the pass, was already structurally excluded. Next time a slice classifies or keys on file-name text, make the design's cases list include a fuzz or look-alike-character case for the totality claim, and don't spend critique majors on writer concurrency in Core analysis passes.
learned.evidence: O-020: clip.m<U+212A>v threw ArgumentException from Dictionary.Add, found only by code review 1. Critique M1 and M2 (no writer) were overridden on Scanner.cs:66/312 and MainWindow.xaml.cs:257. Validate's independent fuzz then covered every UTF-16 unit as an extension.

learned.lesson: Never pair an OrdinalIgnoreCase dictionary with keys made by ToLowerInvariant. Equality under the comparer is not identity under lowering. On the pinned .NET 10.0.12 the real collisions are U+212A→k, U+212B→å, U+2126→ω and U+1E9E→ß. Also probe on the runtime before writing a test from a reviewer's example: the review's U+01C5/U+01C6 digraph does not collide.
learned.evidence: Build 2 probe: OrdinalIgnoreCase says False for the four real pairs and True for U+01C6/U+01C5. Mutation check: with the lowered lookup disabled, the new Fact fails with 'An item with the same key has already been added. Key: .mkv'.

learned.lesson: The critique's claims about App lifecycle and test tooling were mostly wrong, because the recorded stack line lags the code (it lists FSA_HOOK_MODE as stop|throw|close, but rescan has existed since SL-040). Six of the ten findings were overridden after someone read code the critique had not opened. Before any design or critique that touches scan-end behaviour, give it the actual hook-mode list in StartupHook.cs, the scan-end handler in MainWindow.xaml.cs, and the real definition of T-005.
learned.evidence: M1, M2, M4, m1, m4 and m5 were overridden citing MainWindow.xaml.cs:257 and :442-446, Scanner.cs:66/312, StartupHook.cs:51-59, ScanStore.Rollup.cs:42-47 and WindowCases.ps1:2536-2576. M4 claimed no hook mode can write a report mid-scan or start a rescan, and rescan does exactly that.

learned.lesson: A critique's fix text turns into build work verbatim. Before a fix names an assertion in an existing window case, check that the case reaches that path. C-012's throw mode deletes the report in StartReportMode before the window exists, so a 'no kinds' assertion there can never fail.
learned.evidence: Build 1 discharged O-018 on a C-012 plant that proved nothing about kinds (App.xaml.cs:66 File.Delete, exit 70 at :84-89). Code review 1 m1 caught it, and build 2 restored C-012 and moved coverage to B-001 and K-003 through ShowProblem.

learned.lesson: Any new App column that formats a number must call the shared formatter, not restate it. ShareText.Percent (src/FsAnalyser.App/ShareText.cs) is now the only percentage formatter and is linked into Core.Tests. WPF-free App text classes get unit-tested by linking them into Core.Tests.csproj, not by a window case. A design should name the formatter for every new column, not only the size one.
learned.evidence: O-022: build 1 copied SL-044's review-m2 rounding rule (AwayFromZero, F1, ' %') into KindRowText. The design's 'reuses the size formatter' line said nothing about the percent rule.

learned.lesson: Real-drive numbers to design from. C: has 3,021 distinct extensions (2,958 unmapped, none first seen past 4,096, and the cap is now 65,536). After the map changes, Other is 23.17% of on-disk bytes on C:, close to the design's 23.6% arithmetic, and no-extension is 17.63%. On D:, Other is 46%. The map does not fit every drive, so don't re-open the 25% threshold from the spike. The design chose to itemize Other instead of tuning the map, and this slice did not settle whether that is enough.
learned.evidence: O-016 measurement; build-2 C: run (Programs 26.78%, Other 23.17%, No extension 17.63%); validate D: run (Other 46%).

learned.lesson: Drive totals move between runs, so reconcile kinds only against the core totals of the same scan, never against a figure quoted by an earlier stage.
learned.evidence: C: file counts were 3,642,758 (spike), 3,630,383 (build 2) and 3,614,900 (validate). Each run's ten kinds still summed exactly to that run's core totals.

learned.lesson: The loop has no gate that looks at a screen. Every finding (10 critique, 3 code review) and the one open design question were settled by a model, and validate's 'not reached' list is where the on-screen check landed. For a slice whose deliverable is text a person reads (PS-005, 'See what kinds of files are in there'), plan a person's look or a screenshot artifact in advance instead of leaving it to validate to report as not reached.
learned.evidence: Validate: extensions-column text, trimming and the Installers/Programs tooltip were checked only through KindRowText unit tests. On D:, whether Other's itemization is informative was never seen. The design halted on one question (installers) and a model accepted the default while the owner was away.

learned.lesson: SynchronousIoCancelTests.CancelIsResentWhileACallBlocksAgainAfterACancel is intermittently red under load ('call still blocked 2 s after Cancel'). Rerun that class before treating a red there as a regression from the slice at hand.
learned.evidence: It failed once in the build-check baseline (239/240). The class then passed 25/25 on rerun, and it passed in build 2's 260/260 and in validate.

what_went_wrong: The design paired an OrdinalIgnoreCase dictionary with lowercased keys ('allocates its lowercased key once') and promised Compute never throws on odd names. Build 1 shipped a crash: 'clip.m<U+212A>v' threw from Dictionary.Add, exiting 70 in report mode and killing the process interactively, which loses a scan that took minutes. All of build 1's tests were green because the mixed-case matrix (C-001) fed ASCII case only. Code review 1 caught it, and that cost build 2 and a third review round.

The critique aimed its two strongest majors (M1, M2) at the no-writer precondition, which the code already excludes, and none at totality, which the same design listed as must-verify and which then failed. Six of its ten findings were overridden after someone read code the critique had not opened, including M4's claim that no hook mode can start a rescan.

Critique m3's fix, 'add that assertion to the existing throw window case', was carried out as written. Build 1 discharged O-018 on a C-012 plant that the harness deletes before any kinds code runs, so the check could not fail. Code review 1 found it, and the fix was rework.

Build 1 copied the SL-044 percentage-rounding rule into KindRowText instead of reusing it. The design named the size formatter but not the percent formatter, so the drift went unnoticed until code review.

Code review 1's own example was wrong. U+01C5 and U+01C6 do not collide under OrdinalIgnoreCase, and build 2 had to probe the runtime to correct the record. Only the four other code points were real collisions.

The build-check halted on 'partial' when nothing existed, which is the expected verdict for a new feature, and it changed no scope. The design's Installers question was resolved by a model taking the default. No person triaged any critique or code-review finding, and none saw the panel on screen.

Validate's broad totality fuzz lived in a scratch folder under %TEMP% that was deleted afterwards. The repo keeps only the single-shape Fact for the Kelvin-sign case, so the 199,663-check evidence cannot be re-run.

missed.what: The design specified a Dictionary<string,int>(OrdinalIgnoreCase) whose new unmapped keys are added as lowercased strings, and it did not ask whether a name that misses under OrdinalIgnoreCase can lower onto a key already present. KELVIN SIGN U+212A lowers to 'k', so 'clip.m<U+212A>v' misses '.mkv' but lowers to '.mkv', and Dictionary.Add throws. That contradicts the Compute contract ('does not throw on odd names') and the must-verify totality precondition. The design's case list held only ASCII case variants and a trailing-dot or dotfile shape. Check to write: for every comparer-plus-key-transform pair in a design, enumerate non-ASCII characters that the transform maps into the comparer's equivalence class.
missed.caught_by: code-review attempt 1 (M1), fixed in build attempt 2 with FindLowered and a stack-buffer lowered lookup

missed.what: Critique m3 prescribed 'add that assertion to the existing throw window case', which asserts that a faulted run leaves no kinds. The throw mode exits 70 after StartReportMode deletes the report path at App.xaml.cs:66, before the window exists, so the assertion cannot fail on anything to do with kinds. The critique did not check that the target case reaches the code under test.
missed.caught_by: code-review attempt 1 (m1), after build 1 had already discharged O-018 on it

missed.what: The design said the panel's size text reuses the existing formatter but said nothing about the new Share column's percentage rule. SL-044 review m2 had already fixed that rule (one decimal, MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero, ' %'), so build 1 re-implemented it in KindRowText, leaving two copies. Check to write: for each new column in a design, name the existing formatter it must call.
missed.caught_by: code-review attempt 1 (m2), consolidated into ShareText.Percent in build attempt 2

unknowns: Is an Installers row limited to package formats (.msi/.msix/.appx and similar), with setup .exe files counted under Programs, what the person wants for PS-005? Only a name rule (6.5% of Downloads installer bytes) and a model's default have answered it.

Does the top-3-plus-remainder itemization make Other informative on screen? On D:, Other holds 46% of on-disk bytes. Nobody looked at the extensions column or the Installers/Programs tooltip in the running window.

How long does the whole scan-end UI block (tree swap, largest-files pass and kinds pass) take in the app on a real 3.6M-file C: scan? Only the 144-187 ms spike figure and build's 118 ms figure exist, and T-005 samples small trees.

What should the interactive app do when a post-scan pass throws? Code review 1 states that App.OnStartup installs no DispatcherUnhandledException handler outside report mode, while the m3 disposition relied on 'the App routes bugs to its failure handler'. Which is true was not settled.

Should a file whose extension uses a compatibility letter (KELVIN SIGN in 'clip.m<U+212A>v') count under the ASCII kind it lowers to, as it does now, or under Other? NTFS and the shell treat it as a different extension.

candidates.title: Promote the O-001 totality fuzz into Core.Tests
candidates.why: Validate's fuzz (every UTF-16 unit as an extension in three case orders, look-alike letters for every mapped extension, 3,000 random stores, a store past the cap) was the only broad evidence that Compute and FileKinds.Of are total. It ran from a deleted %TEMP% scratch project, and the repo keeps only the single-shape Kelvin Fact. Include the weakened-oracle check that produced 14 disagreements.

candidates.title: A person looks at the kinds panel on real C: and D: and rules on the open product choices
candidates.why: The visual check was not reached. The choices settled by model defaults are Installers as package formats only, Kelvin-sign extensions counted as ASCII, ts not a video, no-extension as its own row, and dotfiles in Other. D: Other at 46% on-disk is the case to look at.

candidates.title: Decide what interactive mode does when a post-scan pass throws
candidates.why: The Kelvin crash showed that a throw in ShowKinds (or in any scan-end pass) kills the process and loses a finished scan, because no DispatcherUnhandledException handler is installed outside report mode. The m3 disposition ruled out a catch on the reasoning that the App routes bugs to its failure handler. Reconcile the two.

candidates.title: Per-extension drill-down or full extension table for a kind, starting with Other
candidates.why: This slice deliberately ships no drill-down, only the top 3 extensions plus a remainder. On D:, Other is 46% of on-disk bytes and the design's answer to that is unseen on screen. Rank it after the visual review says whether the itemization is enough.

candidates.title: Measure the whole scan-end UI block on a real 3.6M-file C: scan
candidates.why: Critique m4 (kinds pass on the UI thread) was overridden by reading T-005's definition, not by measuring. Validate did not time Compute inside the app, and the report carries no duration, so the combined tree swap, largest-files and kinds stall at real scale is unmeasured.

candidates.title: Add a hook mode that makes Scanner.Scan throw, for an end-to-end 'Scan failed' window case
candidates.why: The Scan failed ending (Scan throws, then ShowProblem, then HideKinds) is driven by no case. It is covered only through the shared ShowProblem path via B-001 and K-003, and the gap is declared in the WindowCases header.

candidates.title: Deflake SynchronousIoCancelTests.CancelIsResentWhileACallBlocksAgainAfterACancel
candidates.why: It failed once in the build-check baseline ('call still blocked 2 s after Cancel') and passed on every rerun. It guards the cancel path this project depends on most, and an intermittent red there invites someone to dismiss a real regression.
